newsitem.title: UK: British Queen signs order proroguing parliament.
newsitem.headline: British Queen signs order proroguing parliament.

text.p: Britain's Queen Elizabeth has already signed an order proroguing parliament on Friday, government sources said on Wednesday.

They said the queen signed on Wednesday morning while opposition politicians were urging Prime Minister John Major to defer prorogation to give time for a report on allegations that Conservative MPs accepted cash for questions to be published.
The move stops parliamentary business although parliament will not be officially dissolved until April 8.

The House of Commons speaker Betty Boothroyd told MPs earlier that it would be against parliamentary rules for the Standards and Privileges Committee to meet after parliament is prorogued to consider the report.

Labour and Liberal Democrat leaders have urged Major to allow the report to be published to allay suspicions that he arranged for an unusually long period between prorogation and an election in order to ensure it did not appear before polling day.
Major on Monday announced May 1 as the date for the election.
